fixes.explanation: Hiding in Abram's tent isn't what the text says, friend. Genesis 16:6 says Sarai treated Hagar so harshly that “she fled from her.” I think this part hurts, because Hagar was treated so badly that she ran. Then verse 7 says the angel of the LORD found her by a spring in the desert.

That name does show up later in Moses' story, where God is called the God of the fathers (Exodus 3:15). But it isn't the name Hagar gives. In Genesis 16:13 she says, “You are the God who sees me,” about the LORD who spoke to her at the spring. Her name for Him is all about being seen.

Eighty-six is it, and you've got Abram's age on the dot. Genesis 16:16 says, “Abram was eighty-six years old when Hagar bore Ishmael to him.” I can't even remember what I did last year, and you're out here with exact ages. I'm proud of you, baker.

Ninety-nine, friend? You jumped ahead like someone sneaking a taste of the dough before the batch is even mixed! That number does belong to Abram later, in Genesis 17:1. But Genesis 16:16 says, “Abram was eighty-six years old when Hagar bore Ishmael to him.” Keep that ninety-nine in your apron pocket, because it's coming.
